"What's good enough for Elliott ought to be good enough for us!" So retorted an onlooking Belgravian when several competitors in the Club 10 had the effrontery to complain of the hazards and difficulties presented by the crossing of the brook.
John Gladwin anxious for a fast time to gain selection for the European Championships in August held on to Elliott and achieved a seasons best in second place.

Unfortunately, with Elliott and McGeorge finding top form in the 800m and only 2 to be sent for each event, things looked bleak for John. As things turned out the Junior AAA's Championships at Brighton Arena held on represented his last opportunity to gain selection.

It undoubtedley upset John's rhythm and a lap or so later he was not ideally placed when Elliott and Cook kicked for home. Nevertheless our man finished as quickly as the two ahead of him, if not as fast as Ovett who had rejoined the race, (Elliott 2.21.92 Cook 2.22.13 J Gladwin 2.23.18 Morrell 2.23.43 Ovett 2.23.81)

1500m- In the public eye, this event was notable for Elliott's defeat of the eventual Olympic Champion but for Belgrave supporters, attention was focused on Stuart Paton's attempt to make up for his disappointment of last year when not fully fit.
